title: Forced electrogenic and gap junction expression could make unicells form bodies

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Forced electrogenic and gap junction expression could make unicells form bodies

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The proposed role of bioelectrics in multicellularity predicts that forcing expression of appropriate electrogenic proteins and gap junctions in a unicellular organism should induce metazoan-like bodies, and that appropriate changes of bioelectric dynamics may dissolve a metazoan body.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Predictions and Research Program

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The proposed crucial role of bioelectrics in multicellularity predicts that it should be possible to induce the formation of metazoan-like bodies in an otherwise unicellular organism by forcing the expression of appropriate electrogenic proteins and gap junctions. Similarly, it may be possible to induce dissolution of an entire metazoan body by appropriate changes of bioelectric dynamics.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Predictions and Research Program”. Scope: Unicellular organisms engineered with electrogenic proteins and gap junctions; metazoan bodies

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-28: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Both directional predictions have observable outcomes and strong intervention logic. They call for specific engineering and organismal perturbations not supplied by current public data, so they require new experiments.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Engineer a unicellular organism with specified electrogenic and junctional proteins and quantify stable multicellular body formation, differentiation, and coordinated morphology; separately perturb bioelectric dynamics in a metazoan and measure reversible body disintegration.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Appropriate proteins and a metazoan-like body criterion are underspecified.

The required engineered organisms and matched controls are not known to exist publicly.

fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Induction of a body-like form by a named class of genes is a direct gain-of-function test, and failure in controls would be decisive. Genomes tell which genes a unicell already has and do not contain the forcing experiment. The dissolution half is likewise untested in open data. The prediction is clear and awaits the experiment.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Force a defined set of electrogenic proteins and gap junctions in a unicellular species and score emergence of a stable, patterned, multi-cell body against transgenic controls; the converse is a bioelectric manipulation that disperses an existing metazoan body. Body formation only in the forced-expression arm would support the induction prediction; no change, or bodies in the controls, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Dissolving a metazoan body is a separate intervention with no deposited trial.

Metazoan-like needs a pre-specified morphology, or any clump will count.

No public experiment forces this gene set and scores body-like morphogenesis.

analysis feasibility: 0.2

data existence: 0.22
